html: The Mandjindja, also called Mantjintjarra, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Western Desert in Western Australia. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. They belong to the Western Desert cultural bloc. Their neighbours included the Ngaanyatjarra to the north, the Nyanganyatjara to the south, the Tjalkanti to the west and the Nakako to the east. Like other desert peoples they moved between rockholes and soaks, and many had their first lasting contact with Europeans only in the 20th century.
